sugestoes.texto: WHAT: order() copies $val verbatim into -webkit-box-ordinal-group/-moz-box-ordinal-group. WHY: Legacy 2009 box ordinal-group is 1-indexed while order is 0-indexed, so order(2)/order(3) used in header/topic render one slot off on old WebKit/Firefox and defeat the claimed prefix coverage.

WHAT: Removed &.bullet{margin-top:5px} while parent stays float-based, not flex. WHY: The 5px compensation for the floated bullet is lost on topic pages where order() is a no-op, shifting bullet badges up relative to title text.

issues.descricao: Claims the order mixin's box-ordinal-group values are off by one versus order, so legacy WebKit/Firefox render a different item order.
Making .small-action a flex container is claimed to make the floated buttons ignore float:right, because they would be flex items, so they collapse next to the description.

States that the link fallback in PollFeed is correct; no problem is reported.
States the raw_html cook_method comparison in Post#cook is safe; no problem is reported.
States the cook_method assignment in PostCreator is correct; no problem is reported.
States the `if topic_id` check in EmbedController is safe; no problem is reported.
Describes the host checks in ensure_embeddable without reporting a problem.
States content_sha1 and absolutize_urls in TopicEmbed are correct; no problem is reported.
States the TopicRetriever throttle uses setnx and an explicit no_throttle check; no problem is reported.
Claims import_remote passes an unvalidated user-supplied URL to Kernel#open, allowing command execution with '|' or local file reads.
Claims PollFeed fetches SiteSetting.feed_polling_url without validation, letting whoever controls that setting make the server request arbitrary internal or external URLs.
Claims the embed best.html.erb template closes its if block with `end if`, which is invalid Ruby, so every render raises a SyntaxError.
The embed layout interpolates request.referer into an inline JavaScript string with only HTML escaping, so a referer containing a quote can break out of the string and run script.
Claims postMessage drops the resize message because targetOrigin is the full referer URL rather than just the origin, breaking iframe auto-resize.
Claims setting X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL on the embed endpoint disables clickjacking protection and that the referer check can be spoofed.
Claims the cook_method migration default of 1 equals raw_html, so every post would skip cooking and sanitization.
Claims the 'not a url' TopicRetriever spec passes regardless of the InvalidURIError rescue because embeddable_host is blank.
`<%- end if %>` in embed/best.html.erb is not valid Ruby, so the template raises a SyntaxError and the embed page fails to render.
Claims `<%- end if %>` leaves a dangling if modifier that makes the logo output the condition, so the logo renders before the header button.
Claims the embed best action builds the view for current_user and then marks it publicly cacheable, so a staff member's view could be served to anonymous visitors.
fetch_http calls SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase without a presence check, raising NoMethodError when the setting is blank.
poll_feed opens the feed URL without a timeout and imports every item without a cap, so a slow or huge feed can tie up a worker.
The TopicRetriever specs mock perform_retrieve, so a bug in invalid_host? would not make them fail.
The EmbedController success tests only assert that mocks are called and would pass even if the controller logic were removed.
poll_feed has no test of feed parsing or TopicEmbed.import; the specs only check the execute guards.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: website_name parses URI(website.to_s) up to four times per serialization. WHY: Repeated URI parsing is wasted work on a per-user serialization path; the host and path can be read from a single parsed object. HOW: Parse once at the start and reuse the URI object, e.g. uri = URI(website.to_s) rescue nil; return if uri.nil?; website_host = uri.host; return if website_host.nil?; then use uri.path in the branches.

issues.descricao: The www.example.com vs forum.example.com branch of website_name is not tested.
The scheme-less website case (nil host) of website_name is not tested.
Claims the suffix check `"." << website_host` mutates website_host by prepending a dot, so unrelated domains are displayed as ".example.com" and the new unrelated-domain spec fails.
website_name parses the website with URI and returns nil when there is no scheme, so a website like example.com/user disappears from the profile.
The same-domain website label concatenates only host and path, dropping the query string and fragment so the label differs from the link.
Claims website_name silently swallows URI parse errors without logging.

sugestoes.texto:
WHAT: The anchor pattern Pattern.compile("]*>") matches any tag whose name begins with 'a', such as ,
, and , not just anchor tags. WHY: Non-anchor 'a' tags are treated as anchors, so the verifier can emit misleading "Didn't find anchor tag" errors, or silently strip a non-anchor tag before the HTML policy runs when English contains the same tag. HOW: Require a word boundary after the 'a', e.g., ]*)?>, so only , , and are matched.

issues.descricao: Claims santizeAnchors consumes English matcher groups without validation, so a translation with more anchor tags than the English text gets incorrect results.
Notes that normalizeValue blanks the whole choice expression, so a wrong argument index inside the choice would not be flagged.
Claims the English-file path rewrite is fragile and that a messages file without an English counterpart aborts the build with a RuntimeException.
Notes no test covers allowed tags under POLICY_SOME_HTML, so emptying the allow-list would not fail the suite.
VerifyMessageProperties loads message bundles with PropertyResourceBundle(InputStream), claimed to decode as ISO-8859-1 and produce mojibake and spurious Illegal HTML failures for non-English files.
The message verifier compares English files against themselves, so any anchor tag in an English source, including an unsafe href, is stripped before the HTML sanitizer check and never reported.
Error messages in the verifier include absolute file paths; the comment states no data-exposure defect was found.

Claims the import() calls in the appStore object load every app eagerly and should be thunks; the asynchronous loading works as intended.
The commented example entry in app-store/index.ts points to ./example instead of ./_example.
Claims getVideoAdapters performs N sequential module-load round trips per request; the imports already started in parallel at module load.

sugestoes.texto: Bash resolves `../.env` against the directory the script is run from, not the script's own directory. Running `./scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh` from the repo root creates or edits a `.env` in the folder above the repo, so the app never sees `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL`. Build the path from the script's location instead.

HOW: Persist and rehydrate the hashed secretData (and consumed-code state) instead of regenerating it from the raw list on each read.

Recovery codes are sent to user storage providers in plaintext instead of hashed, so a provider may persist working second-factor codes.
The test user storage accepts any of the user's recovery codes rather than the specific requested code number, unlike the local provider.
BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials dereferences getMyUser(user) without a null check, so it throws NullPointerException for a user missing from the provider's map.
Claims recovery code verification compares hashes with String.equals, enabling timing attacks.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: `get_environment_info` calls `issue.get_recommended_event()` for each issue while building the PR comment. WHY: Each call runs a Snuba query and falls back to a second `get_latest_event` query, so one comment costs up to about 10 sequential Snuba round trips for 5 issues. This adds latency to the PR-comment Celery task, and a failure is swallowed and logged at info level. HOW: Fetch environments for all issue ids in one batched query, or use a cheaper source such as the group's latest event environment.

issues.descricao: Claims the unauthenticated endpoint iterates an unbounded array of reports, allowing CPU/metric-spam DoS.

BaseDetectorTypeValidator.update() reads validated_data.get('detector_type') instead of 'type', so detector type changes are silently ignored.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: Service.Check consults permDenialCache before permCache and returns false immediately on a hit, with no revalidation path. WHY: When a user is denied and then granted permission within shortCacheTTL (30 seconds), subsequent Check calls hit the cached denial and return false, even though the permission cache would have fallen back to the database. HOW: Move the permDenialCache lookup after the permCache hit path so cached permissions take precedence, and only consult/store the denial cache when the permission cache has no data or the database confirms a denial.

issues.descricao: Claims a cached denial blocks access granted within the TTL window; denials are TTL-bounded like the existing permission cache.
Claims trusting cached grants while re-checking cached denials lets stale grants keep access to revoked resources; cached grants were already served for the TTL before this PR.
Claims per-resource denial entries cause unbounded cache memory growth; entries expire after the short TTL.
Claims List now serves stale cached permissions whereas it previously always queried the DB; List was already cache-backed before the change.

Claims the new denial cache is checked before any permission source and never invalidated, so a Check that ran before a resource was created or a grant was added keeps returning Allowed:false for the whole short cache TTL.
Claims the remote authz client still wraps results in a 30s LocalCache, so in remote deployments new dashboards, folders and grants stay invisible for up to 30s.
Claims permissionCacheUsage counts a cache hit that did not grant access as a cache miss.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: ContextualLoggerMiddleware is unconditionally added to the middleware stack even when backend request logging is disabled. WHY: When cfg.PluginLogBackendRequests is false, NewLoggerMiddleware returns next and bypasses itself, so the attributes added by ContextualLoggerMiddleware are never consumed, yet every plugin request still pays for the slice allocation and context.WithValue call. HOW: only append NewContextualLoggerMiddleware() when cfg.PluginLogBackendRequests is true, or move the contextual logger creation inside/before LoggerMiddleware so it runs only when logging is enabled.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: the `immediateDelete` branch POSTs the SendGrid cancel and returns without deleting the `WorkflowReminder` row. WHY: the reschedule caller at handleNewBooking.ts:968 passes `immediateDelete=true` and there is no cascade cleanup for a reschedule (the old booking and workflow step are kept), so the old EMAIL reminder row is orphaned forever — it keeps `scheduled: true`, `referenceId` set, and `cancelled` null, so neither cron query in scheduleEmailReminders.ts matches it. HOW: after the SendGrid cancel, delete the row: `await prisma.workflowReminder.delete({ where: { id: reminderId } });`.

WHAT: the new `remindersToCancel` query selects `cancelled: true` rows without excluding a null `referenceId`, unlike the analogous query at workflows.tsx:205 that adds `NOT: { referenceId: null }`. WHY: cancelled rows can have a null referenceId (any reminder never given a SendGrid batch id), and those are sent to SendGrid as `batch_id: null`, which fails the request and — since the whole loop shares one try/catch — aborts cancellation of the remaining reminders. HOW: add `NOT: { referenceId: null }` to the `where` clause of the `remindersToCancel` query.

The new cancelled column is nullable without a default, so existing WorkflowReminder rows get null instead of false.

The reschedule path cancels SendGrid email reminders immediately (immediateDelete=true) instead of flagging them cancelled for the cron, which supposedly accumulates cancelled batches.
When an email reminder is cancelled immediately on reschedule, its WorkflowReminder row is never deleted or marked cancelled, so stale scheduled reminder rows are left in the database.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: `createInitialDeployment` returns early when `updateStrategy` is null, so the `rolling-updates` preview feature is never enabled for that parameterized test case. WHY: The documentation says the operator fails while the feature is in preview if it is not enabled, and the null-strategy branch is still intended to exercise update behavior, so the test may fail or silently test an unsupported configuration. HOW: Move the feature-spec setup before the null-strategy early return, or remove the early return and always install the enabled feature.

WHAT: The new `rolling-updates` feature enabling code is unreachable when `updateStrategy` is null because of the early return at line 105. WHY: `upgradeStrategy()` supplies `null` as a parameter, so the null-strategy test cases deploy Keycloak without enabling the required preview feature, causing them to exercise the wrong behavior or fail. HOW: Move the `FeatureSpec` creation and `setEnabledFeatures(...)` call before the `if (updateStrategy == null) { return kc; }` block, or remove the early return.

issues.descricao: Claims the rolling-updates feature is not enabled for the null update strategy in UpgradeTest, so that case tests the operator without the gated feature.
Claims RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE changed from 4 to 3 and 4 now means feature disabled, a breaking change that needs release notes.
Claims calling picocli.exit() for the disabled-feature exit code is incorrect because it calls System.exit directly.
Claims `Profile.isFeatureEnabled` in UpdateCompatibilityCheck can hit a null profile and throw NullPointerException because initProfile is skipped for update-compatibility.

sugestoes.texto: Making `.small-action-desc` a content-sized flex item causes its right-floated edit/delete buttons to sit beside short descriptions instead of at the right edge of the action row. Give `.small-action-desc` `flex: 1` (with the corresponding supported prefixes) so it fills the space remaining after the avatar.

issues.descricao: Claims the order mixin's box-ordinal-group values are off by one versus order, so legacy WebKit/Firefox render a different item order.
Making .small-action a flex container is claimed to make the floated buttons ignore float:right, because they would be flex items, so they collapse next to the description.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: The early return for null strategy skips enabling the `rolling-updates` preview feature, so default-strategy tests deploy without it. WHY: Leaves null-parameterized cases exercising a configuration the docs declare invalid and asymmetric with the RECREATE cases. HOW: Move the FeatureSpec enabling before the null check.

issues.descricao: Claims the rolling-updates feature is not enabled for the null update strategy in UpgradeTest, so that case tests the operator without the gated feature.
Claims RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE changed from 4 to 3 and 4 now means feature disabled, a breaking change that needs release notes.
Claims calling picocli.exit() for the disabled-feature exit code is incorrect because it calls System.exit directly.
Claims `Profile.isFeatureEnabled` in UpdateCompatibilityCheck can hit a null profile and throw NullPointerException because initProfile is skipped for update-compatibility.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: FallbackLocaleList#[] hits SiteSetting.default_locale on every fallback resolution. WHY: Fallback lookup runs per missing translation so each request pays repeated setting lookups instead of one cached read.

issues.descricao: Claims a fallback value cached for a not-yet-loaded locale stays stale after that locale's file is loaded, because ensure_loaded! does not invalidate the translation cache.
Suggests normalizing the locale because a String locale mixed with Symbol fallback entries defeats uniq and causes double lookups or double loading.
Claims a nil default_locale makes FallbackLocaleList#[] raise NoMethodError on every missing translation.
Claims every fallback lookup hits the database or Redis through SiteSetting.default_locale, amplifying per-request load.
Claims a user-controlled locale with regex metacharacters reaches load_locale's Regexp and forces loading of unintended locale files.
Claims @loaded_locales is lazily initialized and shared across threads without synchronization.
I18n.ensure_loaded! reads and initializes @loaded_locales outside LOAD_MUTEX, racing with reload!/load_locale under concurrent requests.
Claims set_locale's `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` (application_controller.rb:159) raises NoMethodError on every request if I18n.fallbacks is not the custom FallbackLocaleList.
FallbackLocaleList subclasses Hash but leaves it empty, so iterating I18n.fallbacks returns nothing.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: readLength returns -1 when it encounters the BER indefinite-length marker 0x80. WHY: DER requires definite lengths, so accepting -1 leads to NegativeArraySizeException in readInteger or an empty sequence in readSequence instead of a clear malformed-input error. HOW: Throw an IOException rejecting indefinite-length encoding.

WHAT: readSequence subtracts each element's full byte length from the declared sequence length without checking the element fits. WHY: A malformed element larger than the remaining sequence length can underflow length and exit the loop silently, returning a sequence with fewer elements than declared and masking the corruption. HOW: Validate that bytes.length <= length before subtracting, and verify length reaches exactly 0 after the loop.

issues.descricao: Claims getBouncyCastleProvider returns the JDK keystore provider instead of BouncyCastle; that is the intended fallback for the BC-free authz client.
Claims readLength's -1 for indefinite-length encoding breaks length arithmetic or array allocation; the decoder only parses locally generated DER and the sequence path already rejects it.
Claims the lenient sequence parser allows malformed or trailing DER and signature malleability in verification; the parser never sees external signatures.
Claims integerToBytes can silently truncate oversized INTEGER values; inputs come from local signing and always fit the component width.
Claims createECParams/getKeyFactory throwing UnsupportedOperationException breaks EC JWK parsing in the authz client; the client does not use that path.

ASN1Decoder.readInteger passes the -1 returned by readLength for indefinite-length encoding to read(int), which allocates new byte[-1] and throws an unchecked NegativeArraySizeException instead of an IOException on malformed DER input.
integerToBytes silently truncates r/s values longer than the curve size, so non-canonical DER signatures are accepted as different values (signature malleability).
AuthzClient.create eagerly initializes CryptoIntegration, so a shaded/repackaged client that lost its ServiceLoader file fails at construction instead of only when ECDSA is used.

Calling CryptoIntegration.init from AuthzClient.create is claimed to lock the global crypto provider to the minimal AuthzClientCryptoProvider so a later server init is ignored and unsupported operations fail.
The ignored-providers message is passed to logger.debugf as a format string instead of using logger.debug, and keeps a trailing comma.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: ClientPermissionsV2 overrides setPermissionsEnabled, isPermissionsEnabled, resource, and getPermissions to throw UnsupportedOperationException. WHY: V1 paths such as the client-removal cleanup listener (AdminPermissions.java:88-91) and the /management/permissions endpoint (ClientResource.java:709-742) still invoke these methods; when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled, AdminPermissions.management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2, causing client deletion and the permissions endpoint to fail with an internal error. HOW: implement V2 equivalents for these methods or make the V1 callers guard against V2 before invoking them.

issues.descricao: Claims the per-client resource lookup uses server.getId() as owner while resources are created with server.getClientId(), so client-specific permissions are never found.
Claims that with both fine-grained features enabled, client deletion calls ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled and throws UnsupportedOperationException.
Claims the all-clients resource lookup in hasPermission(String) cannot find the resource (owner mismatch or not lazily created), so global client permissions are ignored.
Claims the client management-permissions endpoint returns a 500 under V2 because it calls ClientPermissionsV2 methods that throw UnsupportedOperationException.
Claims hasPermission(client, scope) accepts permissions granted on other resources because it does not filter by resource id, allowing privilege escalation across clients.
Claims getClientsWithPermission runs a separate policy evaluation for every client resource, causing O(N) slowdowns.
ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission runs a full policy evaluation for every client resource of type Clients, so listing clients costs one evaluation per client resource.

On ClientRemovedEvent the AdminPermissions listener calls clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false), which throws UnsupportedOperationException in ClientPermissionsV2 when V1 and V2 are both enabled, so client deletion fails.
Claims that with both fine-grained authz V1 and V2 enabled, the ClientRemovedEvent listener calls ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled, which now throws, so client deletion fails.
Claims the test grants CONFIGURE together with MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE, so addComposites may succeed because of CONFIGURE and the test would pass even if canMapCompositeRoles were broken.
Claims that under FGAP V2 the client management-permissions GET/PUT endpoints call the throwing ClientPermissionsV2 overrides and return 500.

ClientPermissionsV2 canMapRoles/canMapCompositeRoles/canMapClientScopeRoles check only fine-grained permissions and not the manage-clients role, claimed to deny role mapping to realm admins unlike V1.
Claims the canView(ClientModel) Javadoc is misleading because V2 never evaluates the per-client VIEW_SCOPE permission.
Claims the tests index getDefaultClientScopes() without size checks and could throw IndexOutOfBoundsException.

sugestoes.texto: The SQL-expression gate is applied only inside `ReadQuery`'s `QueryTypeSQL` case, but `buildCMDNode` reads SQL via `UnmarshalSQLCommand` whenever `FlagExpressionParser` is disabled and the command type is `sql`. Because `FlagExpressionParser` is off by default, the default production path never reaches `ReadQuery` and never hits the gate, so `UnmarshalSQLCommand`->`NewSQLCommand` still builds a live SQLCommand. Apply the SQL expression gate to this nodes.go path as well.

issues.descricao: enableSqlExpressions always returns false regardless of the sqlExpressions feature flag, so SQL expressions are rejected unconditionally.
The go-duck DB was replaced by a stub whose methods always return 'not implemented', so table parsing and SQL expression execution always fail.
Claims the rejection message says 'not implemented' though the guard is a feature-flag check.
Garbled request to update db.go to use sql.NewInMemoryDB().
Vague claim that the query interface changed and lines 96 and 100 need updating.
enableSqlExpressions returns false on every path (the flag is negated and both branches return false), so SQL expressions are rejected even when FlagSqlExpressions is enabled.
Claims TablesList now calls a stub that always errors, so existing parser tests in pkg/expr/sql/parser_test.go would break.
The TypeSQL branch in nodes.go reaches UnmarshalSQLCommand → NewSQLCommand → DuckDB parsing without the enableSqlExpressions check, leaving the SQL expression RCE/LFI path reachable.
Existing SQL tests in sql_command_test.go calling NewSQLCommand would now fail because the stubbed DB's TablesList returns 'not implemented', and they were not updated.
Claims that with the stub DB every SQL expression fails parsing and the raw user SQL is logged verbatim, leaking sensitive data.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: The new missing-encryption-key branch throws instead of returning a JSON error response. WHY: Throwing from the Next API route yields a non-JSON 500 page, so the caller's await response.json() rejects and the UI can only show a generic error with an unhandled server exception. HOW: Return res.status(500).json({ error: ErrorCode.InternalServerError }) like the surrounding branches.

issues.descricao: Claims a caller of the changed TwoFactorAuthAPI.disable still passes two arguments, but that caller uses a different, unchanged API module.
The enable-2FA test asserts toBeTruthy on the un-awaited isChecked() Promise, so it passes regardless of the switch state, including now that the backup-codes step is never dismissed.
Backup codes are compared with indexOf/=== instead of a constant-time comparison, theoretically leaking timing information.
Suggests a clearer post-2FA redirect journey in a file that does not exist.
Claims a 2FA page leaks a polling interval; no such page or interval exists.
Reports no issue.
The first 2FA e2e test asserts toBeTruthy() on an unawaited isChecked() Promise, so it always passes even though the backup-codes step now keeps 2FA unchecked until Close is clicked.
The lost-access/go-back toggle button inside the disable-2FA form lacks type="button", so clicking it is claimed to submit the form and fire handleDisable with empty codes.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: `getCredentials` accesses `myUser.recoveryCodes` without the null guard used by `isConfiguredFor` and `isValid`. WHY: A missing map entry throws NPE during federated credential lookup instead of returning empty. HOW: Return `Stream.empty()` when `myUser` is null.

issues.descricao: Claims the recovery-code validator uses non-constant-time String.equals, leaking timing information about stored codes.
Claims raw recovery codes are serialized and persisted in cleartext in user storage instead of hashed.
Claims Optional.get() on RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user) without isPresent() can throw NoSuchElementException.
Plaintext recovery codes are serialized and sent to user storage providers via updateCredential, while the local path stores only hashed codes.
Recovery codes are sent to user storage providers in plaintext instead of hashed, so a provider may persist working second-factor codes.
The test user storage accepts any of the user's recovery codes rather than the specific requested code number, unlike the local provider.
BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials dereferences getMyUser(user) without a null check, so it throws NullPointerException for a user missing from the provider's map.
Claims recovery code verification compares hashes with String.equals, enabling timing attacks.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: `handleCancelBooking` calls `prisma.credential.findUnique` inside a loop over calendar references. WHY: Cancelling a collective booking issues one credential query per host calendar reference rather than a single batched query. HOW: Collect all `credentialId` values from `bookingCalendarReference`, run one `prisma.credential.findMany({ where: { id: { in: ids } } })`, and map the results.

issues.descricao: Claims GoogleCalendarService.createEvent/updateEvent dereference an undefined mainHostDestinationCalendar when destinationCalendar is null or empty.
destinationCalendar is defaulted to null in some producers and to an empty array in others.
loadUsers no longer selects organization.slug for dynamic-user bookings, so code reading user.organization gets undefined.

Claims that for references without a credentialId, looping over every calendar reference and deleting each against all user calendar credentials produces duplicate or wrong-target delete calls and errors.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: `.small-action-desc` padding changed from a 4em left padding to `0 1.5%`, but `mobile/topic-post.scss` still applies `.small-action .small-action-desc .custom-message { margin-left: -40px; }`, which was tuned for the old 4em padding. WHY: on mobile the custom message is now pulled about 35px left of the description box and overlaps or clips against the avatar icon. HOW: update or remove the mobile `margin-left: -40px` override to match the new padding.

issues.descricao: Claims the order mixin's box-ordinal-group values are off by one versus order, so legacy WebKit/Firefox render a different item order.
Making .small-action a flex container is claimed to make the floated buttons ignore float:right, because they would be flex items, so they collapse next to the description.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: The immediateDelete branch cancels the SendGrid scheduled send then returns without deleting or marking the WorkflowReminder row. WHY: Rescheduled bookings (handleNewBooking) keep a scheduled:true row forever, diverging from the SMS path that deletes and leaking orphan reminders. HOW: Delete the reminder row after the SendGrid cancel before returning.

issues.descricao: The booking-page reschedule path cancels email reminders with immediateDelete=true, which leaves the WorkflowReminder row in the DB, while the dashboard reschedule path marks it cancelled for cleanup, so the two flows are inconsistent.
Claims the code comment overstates the cancel window because the query lacks a lower bound on scheduledDate.
Claims the cron's cancel loop uses an undefined `client` variable, causing a ReferenceError.
Claims the unscheduled-reminders query re-schedules reminders marked cancelled because it lacks a cancelled filter.
Claims a hard-coded "Verification code" placeholder bypasses i18n.
Claims a hard-coded "Verify" button label bypasses i18n.

With immediateDelete=true, deleteScheduledEmailReminder cancels the SendGrid send but neither deletes nor marks the WorkflowReminder row, leaving orphaned scheduled rows inconsistent with the non-immediate path.
Claims reminders from disabled event types are still sent and can be re-scheduled because they are only marked cancelled.
Notes the isSenderIdNeeded branch removal without reporting a problem.
The new cancelled column is nullable without a default, so existing WorkflowReminder rows get null instead of false.

With immediateDelete=true, deleteScheduledEmailReminder cancels the SendGrid batch and returns without deleting or flagging the WorkflowReminder row, and the callers no longer delete it, so reminder rows are left orphaned in the database.
The reschedule path cancels SendGrid email reminders immediately (immediateDelete=true) instead of flagging them cancelled for the cron, which supposedly accumulates cancelled batches.
When an email reminder is cancelled immediately on reschedule, its WorkflowReminder row is never deleted or marked cancelled, so stale scheduled reminder rows are left in the database.
